lanes.auditor_hypothesis: Aggressive multi-day-persistent options sweeps work as a short-term directional momentum signal; Pan & Poteshman 2006 shows the predictive option-volume signal comes ONLY from buy-to-open volume at ~40bps next day / ~1% per week; sweep-style aggressive prints predict returns (Hu 2014; Easley-O'Hara-Srinivas 1998); multi-day persistence improves the signal. System keeps this 0-scored/narrative with an OI-confirmed-opening gate capping sizing.
lanes.method: sweep-momentum (multi-day-persistent aggressive options sweeps as short-term directional momentum; OI-confirmed-opening gate per Pan & Poteshman 2006). Verification method: WebSearch on all named papers plus 2023-2026 follow-on work; full-text extraction of Pan & Poteshman 2006 (MIT-hosted PDF, zlib stream extraction after pdftoppm unavailable) to verify the exact decomposition, magnitudes, public-vs-nonpublic results, and trade-type table; arXiv 2201.09319 full text for persistence; abstracts/records for Hu 2014, EOS 1998, Ge-Lin-Pearson 2016, Muravyev 2016, Bryzgalova et al. 2023, Augustin et al. 2019, Muravyev-Pearson-Pollet 2025.

key_citations.cite: Pan, J. & Poteshman, A.M. (2006), Review of Financial Studies 19(3), 871-908, "The Information in Option Volume for Future Stock Prices"
key_citations.finding: Verified from full text. Put-call ratios from OPEN-BUY volume (proprietary CBOE trade-type data, 1990-2001): lowest-quintile P/C stocks outperform highest by >40bps next day and >1% next week on a four-factor risk-adjusted basis (next-day regression slope −53bps in main test, −35bps in PIN subsample); predictability "gradually dies out" over several weeks WITHOUT reversal. Trade-type comparison (Table 9): open-buy is "clearly the most informative," but open-sell IS positive and significant (much weaker), close-sell similar to open-sell, close-buy correct-sign but insignificant — so "ONLY buy-to-open" is an overstatement. Critical: the PUBLICLY observable Lee-Ready-signed version of the signal predicts "only the next one or two trade days," then prices REVERSE (price pressure, not information), and it loses all significance once open-buy is controlled. Predictability stronger with leverage (OTM), in smaller stocks (−5.27bps per unit ln-size), high-PIN stocks (+43bps low→high PIN), and from full-service-broker customers (~70% of open-buy volume).
key_citations.relation: Supports the OI-confirmed-opening gate (opening volume is where the information is) and the headline magnitudes as claimed. Contradicts the strict "ONLY buy-to-open" reading. Heavily qualifies the system usage: a sweep signal inferred from the PUBLIC tape resembles P&P's public Lee-Ready signal — 1-2 day horizon with subsequent reversal — not their non-public 40bps/1% signal.

key_citations.cite: Hu, J. (2014), Journal of Financial Economics 111(3), 625-645, "Does Option Trading Convey Stock Price Information?"
key_citations.finding: Verified. Decomposes stock order imbalance into option-induced (delta-adjusted signed option volume transmitted via market-maker delta hedges) vs option-independent components (sample ~Apr 2008-Aug 2010, ~2,200 optionable stocks/day). Option-induced imbalance significantly predicts cross-sectional stock returns with NO reversal at longer horizons (information, not pressure); option-independent imbalance has only transitory impact. Strongest in informationally opaque firms; predicts CARs 5 days before earnings announcements. Citing work notes predictive power comes mainly from ATM/ITM delta exposure, not OTM. Exact decile bps spreads are paywalled — not independently verifiable from open sources.
key_citations.relation: Supports the premise that aggressive signed option prints carry directional information for the underlying at daily horizons — the closest published analog to a sweep signal — provided flow is delta-weighted and direction-signed.

key_citations.cite: Easley, D., O'Hara, M. & Srinivas, P.S. (1998), Journal of Finance 53(2), 431-465, "Option Volume and Stock Prices: Evidence on Where Informed Traders Trade"
key_citations.finding: Verified. Sequential-trade model with informed venue choice (pooling equilibrium: informed trade in both stock and options when option leverage/liquidity suffice). Empirics: direction-classified "positive news" and "negative news" option volumes predict stock price changes, while total (unsigned) option volume does not. Sample is ~50 CBOE firms over Oct-Nov 1990 at INTRADAY lead-lag horizons — not a daily/swing momentum design.
key_citations.relation: Supports the theoretical foundation (signed option flow leads the stock; unsigned volume is uninformative) but only qualifies the system usage: it is intraday lead-lag evidence, not evidence for multi-day directional momentum.

key_citations.cite: Ge, L., Lin, T.-C. & Pearson, N.D. (2016), Journal of Financial Economics 120(3), 601-622, "Why does the option to stock volume ratio predict stock returns?"
key_citations.finding: Verified. Using ISE signed open/close option volume (commercially available data, unlike P&P's): purchases of calls that OPEN new positions are the strongest return predictor, followed by call sales closing existing purchased positions; O/S negatively predicts next-week returns; embedded leverage is the dominant channel; predictability extends about a week-plus without immediate reversal.
key_citations.relation: Supports — partially rescues the public-replicability problem in P&P (signed open/close data can be licensed) and independently confirms opening-volume primacy, i.e., the system's OI-confirmed-opening gate.

key_citations.cite: Chakravarty, S., Jain, P., Upson, J. & Wood, R. (2012), Journal of Financial and Quantitative Analysis 47(2), 415-435, "Clean Sweep: Informed Trading through Intermarket Sweep Orders"
key_citations.finding: Verified. EQUITY-market ISOs are 46% of trades / 41% of volume, carry significantly larger information share despite smaller size, and post-trade return analysis indicates informed institutions are the main ISO users. Related: Cox (SSRN 3197414) finds equity ISO imbalances predict positive CARs up to two months, strongest in small caps.
key_citations.relation: Qualifies. This is the actual published basis for "sweep = informed urgency," but it is for equities, not options. No peer-reviewed study validating OPTIONS-market sweep prints as a return signal was found — the options-sweep claim rests on extrapolation plus practitioner literature.

key_citations.cite: Muravyev, D. (2016), Journal of Finance 71(2), 673-708, "Order Flow and Expected Option Returns"
key_citations.finding: Verified. Decomposes the price impact of option trades into inventory-risk and asymmetric-information components: both are large, but the INVENTORY component is larger; option order imbalances attributable to inventory have ~5x larger impact on option prices than previously thought; past order imbalances are the strongest predictor of option returns (via mean-reverting inventory effects).
key_citations.relation: Contradicts/qualifies the naive reading: a large fraction of the price action that follows aggressive option prints is dealer inventory pressure that mean-reverts, not information. Momentum-chasing sweeps without an information filter risks buying transient pressure.

key_citations.cite: Bryzgalova, S., Pavlova, A. & Sikorskaya, T. (2023), Journal of Finance 78(6), 3465-3514, "Retail Trading in Options and the Rise of the Big Three Wholesalers"
key_citations.finding: Verified. Documents the post-2019 explosion of retail options trading executed via PFOF wholesalers (~90% of PFOF from three wholesalers); retail concentrates in cheap, short-dated weekly options, pays average effective bid-ask spreads of 12.6%, and loses money on average.
key_citations.relation: Contradicts the modern prior that aggressive ask-side option prints are smart money: in post-2020 data a large share of urgent, market-taking option flow is retail noise. Any sweep signal must separate institutional from retail prints (the system's ≥$500K floor is the right direction).

key_citations.cite: Augustin, P., Brenner, M. & Subrahmanyam, M.G. (2019), Management Science 65(12), 5697-5720, "Informed Options Trading Prior to Takeover Announcements: Insider Trading?"
key_citations.finding: Verified. In 1,859 U.S. takeovers (1996-2012), ~25% show statistically abnormal pre-announcement option volume, concentrated in short-dated OTM calls of targets, accumulating persistently over the ~30 pre-announcement days; over half of the abnormal activity is not explained by speculation, rumors, or disclosed insider activity; SEC litigates ~8% of deals.
key_citations.relation: Supports (indirectly) the multi-day-persistence premise: genuinely informed option flow does build over consecutive days ahead of hard catalysts. But this is event-study evidence of flow persistence, not a test that persistence-filtering improves a tradeable momentum signal.

key_citations.cite: Muravyev, D., Pearson, N.D. & Pollet, J. (2025), Journal of Financial Economics 172, "Why Does Options Market Information Predict Stock Returns?"
key_citations.finding: Verified (published Oct 2025). Shows the classic option-price-based stock-return predictors (implied-vol spread and skew) predict returns largely because they proxy for stock BORROW FEES — a friction that prevents arbitrage — rather than option traders' private information per se.
key_citations.relation: Qualifies (2025, post-cutoff-adjacent). The newest JFE evidence reframes option-market predictability as short-sale-friction proxying. It targets price-based, not volume-based, signals — it does not overturn P&P/Hu/GLP — but warns against interpreting every option-market signal as informed flow; check hard-to-borrow status before reading bearish option flow as information.

key_citations.cite: Michael, N., Cucuringu, M. & Howison, S. (2022), arXiv:2201.09319, "Option Volume Imbalance as a Predictor for Equity Market Returns" (working paper, not peer-reviewed journal)
key_citations.finding: Verified from full text. Using NOM/PHLX daily customer-type-disaggregated signed option volume: customer OVI predicts next-day (especially overnight) stock returns; for top customer-OVI quantiles, cumulative returns over 1-10 day holding periods do NOT mean-revert (persistent, second-day returns still significant, p=0.00); strategy profitability is modest, ~1.3-1.6 bps profit-per-dollar daily out-of-sample; market-maker OVI predicts with opposite sign.
key_citations.relation: Supports both the directional premise and (weakly) the persistence premise on modern (post-2015) public-feed data, while showing realistic magnitudes are bps-scale, far below the 40bps/day of P&P's non-public 1990s signal.

lanes.counter_evidence: Three substantive strands. (1) Pan & Poteshman 2006's OWN public-data result: the Lee-Ready publicly-inferred version of their signal predicts only 1-2 days and then REVERSES, and loses all significance once non-public open-buy volume is controlled — a system reading direction off the public sweep tape is closer to this reversing price-pressure signal than to the famous 40bps/1% non-public one. (2) Muravyev 2016 JF: the inventory-risk component of option order flow price impact exceeds the asymmetric-information component (~5x larger than previously estimated), so aggressive prints partially move prices through mean-reverting dealer inventory pressure, not information. (3) Bryzgalova, Pavlova & Sikorskaya 2023 JF: post-2019, retail dominates urgent short-dated option flow via PFOF wholesalers and loses money on average — eroding the 1990s-2000s-era prior that market-taking option prints are smart money. Additionally: no peer-reviewed study of OPTIONS-market sweep orders specifically was found (the ISO evidence is for equities), no published test that multi-day persistence-filtering improves option-flow signals, and practitioner estimates (Cboe research, 2024, secondary source) put hedge/spread-leg/roll contamination of flagged 'unusual activity' at 30-40%.
nuances_for_plan: Keep sweep-momentum 0-scored/advisory. The published evidence supports signed OPENING option volume as informative, not sweep prints per se; options-sweep-specific predictability has never been validated in a peer-reviewed venue, so promotion to scored points should come only from the system's own calibration audits, never from these citations.

The OI-confirmed-opening gate is the single most evidence-backed element (P&P Table 9: open-buy 'clearly the most informative', close-buy insignificant; Ge-Lin-Pearson 2016 independently confirms opening-purchase primacy). Keep it, and keep the size/OI<0.5 closing anti-signal (C19) — both align with the literature. But stop describing P&P as 'only buy-to-open': open-sell and close-sell volume also carry significant (weaker) information, so sold-to-open puts/calls should not be treated as informationless.

Horizon discipline: on PUBLIC tape, P&P-style signals predict 1-2 days then reverse. Treat un-OI-confirmed sweep momentum as a <=2-session tactical signal with tight invalidation and expect reversal risk; only OI-confirmed (next-day OI build) or multi-day net-premium-confirmed flow earns a swing read (Hu 2014 and GLP 2016 no-reversal results apply to properly signed/confirmed flow).

Multi-day persistence is a plausible-but-unproven enhancer: informed flow demonstrably accumulates across days before hard catalysts (Augustin et al. 2019 M&A evidence), and order-splitting theory predicts it, but generic order-flow persistence is mostly mechanical splitting/herding whose price pressure fades within a day (Lillo-Farmer line). The system's multi-day repeat filter should be validated in /calibration-audit as its own conditional gate, not cited as literature-backed.

Retail contamination is the biggest regime change vs the cited papers' samples (1990-2012): post-2020, urgent short-dated option prints are majority-retail and retail loses money (Bryzgalova et al. 2023). The >=$500K premium floor and common-stock/opening filters in C19 are the right mitigations; additionally down-weight cheap weekly OTM sweeps and small clip sizes when narrating 'smart money'.

Expect inventory-pressure head-fakes (Muravyev 2016): a meaningful share of post-sweep drift is dealer inventory mean-reversion. Prefer delta-adjusted net flow (Hu 2014) over raw premium counts, and note that the predictability in Hu-style imbalance comes mainly from ATM/ITM delta exposure rather than OTM lottery prints — which tensions with the common 'OTM sweeps = conviction' heuristic and with P&P's leverage result; resolve empirically, don't assume.

Realistic magnitude anchor for any future scoring: the famous 40bps/day & 1%/week is a 1990-2001 NON-PUBLIC-data result concentrated in small, high-PIN stocks; modern public-feed replications run bps-per-day (e.g., ~1.3-1.6 bps/$ daily OOS in the 2022 OVI study). Do not calibrate win-rate or sizing expectations to the P&P headline numbers.

Before reading heavy put/bearish option flow as informed (or call skew as bullish), check borrow-fee/HTB status: Muravyev-Pearson-Pollet 2025 JFE shows option-market predictors often proxy short-sale frictions. The system is structurally blind to borrow fees (fz has no borrow-fee field) — treat this as a known blind spot in sweep narratives on heavily-shorted names.

lanes.auditor_hypothesis: Large dark-pool block prints (signed via a proprietary buy-ratio) + OI buildup indicate quiet institutional accumulation predicting single-name upside drift over days-weeks, justifying its status as a +3 heaviest-co-equal scored line. Sub-questions: (a) Zhu 2014 RFS — do informed traders concentrate in or avoid dark pools? (b) Comerton-Forde & Putnins 2015 on dark trading and price discovery; (c) any published evidence that dark-pool prints predict single-name direction given the unsigned-print problem; (d) institutional herding horizons (Sias 2004).

key_citations.cite: Zhu, H. (2014), Review of Financial Studies 27(3): 747-789, "Do Dark Pools Harm Price Discovery?"
key_citations.finding: Theory model: informed traders trade on the same side and therefore face higher non-execution risk in dark pools, so they self-select onto the lit exchange while liquidity/uninformed traders migrate to the dark pool. Under natural conditions adding a dark pool CONCENTRATES price-relevant information on the exchange and improves price discovery (while reducing exchange liquidity).
key_citations.relation: CONTRADICTS the system's core premise. The canonical cite the 'DP prints = smart money' narrative leans on actually predicts dark prints are disproportionately UNINFORMED — informed traders avoid dark pools, they do not concentrate in them. Caveat: informed dark-pool participation rises when value uncertainty is high and signals are noisy, but the baseline mechanism is adverse to the signal.

key_citations.cite: Comerton-Forde, C. & Putnins, T. (2015), Journal of Financial Economics 118(1): 70-92, "Dark trading and price discovery"
key_citations.finding: Empirical (Australian data, IV identification): dark trades are LESS informed than lit trades. Informational-efficiency deterioration begins once non-block dark trading exceeds ~10% of dollar volume; a 0→10% increase in dark trading raises price impact of lit trades by 0.09 bps per $10,000 (~+5% vs median) and a 10→12.5% increase raises spreads ~2.4% (+3.1 bps for the average stock). Critically: "no evidence that block trades in the dark impede price discovery" — dark BLOCKS are the least informed category, benign precisely because they carry little private information.
key_citations.relation: CONTRADICTS. The system scores large dark blocks as the informed-accumulation signal; CFP's block-specific result says dark blocks are the trade category emptiest of information. The verified 10%-of-dollar-volume threshold and bps magnitudes apply to non-block dark flow harming efficiency — a different phenomenon than the system's signal.

key_citations.cite: Nimalendran, M. & Ray, S. (2014), Journal of Financial Markets 17: 230-261, "Informational linkages between dark and lit trading venues"
key_citations.finding: Using proprietary signed data from one crossing network: dark trades in LESS-LIQUID stocks predict returns over the next 15-120 MINUTES, with leakage coming mainly from smaller algorithmic child orders split across venues; large negotiated block crosses and broker-desk trades transmit LESS information to lit venues.
key_citations.relation: QUALIFIES — this is the closest published support that dark prints carry any directional information, but the horizon is intraday minutes (not days-weeks), the informative prints are small algo slices (not large blocks), and the data was signed by the venue (the system must infer sign).

key_citations.cite: Hatheway, F., Kwan, A. & Zheng, H. (2017), Journal of Financial and Quantitative Analysis 52(6): 2399-2427, "An Empirical Analysis of Market Segmentation on U.S. Equity Markets"
key_citations.finding: Dark venues segment order flow by information risk: adverse-selection risk on lit markets is 25-66% higher than on dark venues; dark venues cream-skim uninformed flow via sub-penny price improvement; dark transactions are less informed and contribute less to price discovery.
key_citations.relation: CONTRADICTS — direct U.S. empirical confirmation that the average dark execution is the LESS-informed side of the market, the opposite of the accumulation premise.

key_citations.cite: Sias, R. (2004), Review of Financial Studies 17(1): 165-206, "Institutional Herding"
key_citations.finding: Institutional demand is positively autocorrelated across adjacent QUARTERS (13F data); herding results mostly from institutions inferring information from each other's trades rather than momentum; herded-into stocks do not subsequently reverse at quarterly horizons, consistent with informative herding.
key_citations.relation: QUALIFIES — supports 'institutional accumulation is informed and persistent,' but at quarterly 13F horizons, not the days-weeks drift the system scores; Sias provides no evidence about dark-pool prints or sub-quarter timing.

key_citations.cite: Dasgupta, A., Prat, A. & Verardo, M. (2011), Journal of Finance 66(2): 635-653, "Institutional Trade Persistence and Long-Term Equity Returns"
key_citations.finding: Multi-quarter PERSISTENT institutional trading negatively predicts long-term returns: persistently bought stocks underperform persistently sold stocks at long horizons; effect concentrated in smaller stocks and high-institutional-ownership names.
key_citations.relation: QUALIFIES/CONTRADICTS the extrapolation — sustained institutional accumulation eventually predicts reversal, so 'more weeks of accumulation = more bullish' is wrong at the persistence tail.

key_citations.cite: Hendershott, T., Livdan, D. & Schürhoff, N. (2015), Journal of Financial Economics 117(2): 249-287, "Are institutions informed about news?"
key_citations.finding: Signed institutional order flow (Ancerno) predicts news sentiment, announcement-day returns, and earnings surprises days ahead — institutions are informed at daily-weekly horizons.
key_citations.relation: SUPPORTS the horizon claim only — IF you could observe signed institutional flow, days-weeks predictability exists. But this used proprietary signed data; public DP prints are unsigned, so the result transfers only to the extent the proprietary buy-ratio signing actually works (unvalidated in any published work).

key_citations.cite: Keim, D. & Madhavan, A. (1996), Review of Financial Studies 9(1): 1-36, "The Upstairs Market for Large-Block Transactions"; Madhavan, A. & Cheng, M. (1997), RFS 10(1): 175-203
key_citations.finding: Negotiated (upstairs) blocks with KNOWN direction have permanent price impact (informed), buys more than sells; but price moves up to FOUR WEEKS BEFORE the block print are significantly related to trade size — information leaks while the block is shopped, so impact measured from the print date severely underestimates (and largely predates) the information.
key_citations.relation: QUALIFIES — the only block literature showing directional information requires known trade direction, and shows much of the move happens BEFORE the print; a large block print can mark the end of an accumulation campaign rather than the start of drift.

key_citations.cite: Thomas, J., Zhang, F. & Zhu, W. (2021), Management Science 67(12): 7785-7811, "Dark Trading and Post-Earnings-Announcement Drift"
key_citations.finding: Using the SEC Tick Size Pilot as a quasi-experiment: under-reaction to quarterly earnings (PEAD) INCREASES with dark trading; dark trading reduces liquidity available to arbitrageurs rather than improving price discovery.
key_citations.relation: QUALIFIES — recent (post-cutoff-relevant) evidence that high dark-share names incorporate information SLOWER; offers a defensible alternative conditioning (drift after public news in high-dark-share names) but does not validate DP prints as a standalone directional signal.

key_citations.cite: Brogaard, J. & Pan, J. (2022), Review of Financial Studies 35(5): 2625-2666, "Dark Pool Trading and Information Acquisition"
key_citations.finding: Exploiting the Tick Size Pilot: more dark pool trading causes greater fundamental information acquisition (EDGAR search activity around earnings), i.e., dark pools lower expected trading costs for would-be informed traders and encourage information production.
key_citations.relation: QUALIFIES — softens the pure Zhu prediction (dark pools do interact with informed activity through the information-acquisition channel), but still provides no evidence that individual dark prints can be signed and traded directionally.

lanes.counter_evidence: The strongest published counter-evidence targets the exact mechanism the +3 line assumes. (1) Zhu (2014 RFS): informed traders systematically AVOID dark pools because same-side clustering makes their dark fills unlikely — dark flow is selection-biased toward uninformed liquidity traders. (2) Comerton-Forde & Putnins (2015 JFE): dark trades are measurably less informed than lit trades, and specifically "no evidence that block trades in the dark impede price discovery" — i.e., dark BLOCKS (the system's signal object) are the least informationally loaded category; their harmful-efficiency result kicks in only for NON-block dark flow above ~10% of dollar volume. (3) Hatheway, Kwan & Zheng (2017 JFQA): U.S. dark venues cream-skim uninformed flow; lit adverse selection 25-66% higher than dark. (4) The signing problem is documented: most TRF/dark prints execute at the NBBO midpoint where Lee-Ready-type classification is uninformative (Bartlett & McCrary, NBER w21286), so any proprietary buy-ratio on block prints rests on a classification academia considers unreliable for exactly these trades. (5) Dasgupta, Prat & Verardo (2011 JF): persistent multi-quarter institutional buying predicts long-run UNDERPERFORMANCE. (6) No peer-reviewed study was found that validates dark-pool block prints predicting single-name direction over days-weeks; the only published dark-print predictability is 15-120 minutes, in illiquid names, from small algo slices, with venue-signed data (Nimalendran & Ray 2014). Vendor claims of "60-65% breakout rates" after repeated DP blocks trace to marketing content (TradeAlgo-type guides), not published research. Note: one web-search summary offered citations ("Werner & Brogaard 2023, Journal of Trading, Pre-Earnings Dark Pool Activity"; "RFS 2023 dark pool order imbalance r=0.12") that could not be matched to any real paper — treated as hallucinated and excluded.
nuances_for_plan: Demote or de-co-equalize the +3 weight: the academic base inverts the premise (Zhu 2014 mechanism; CFP 2015 dark blocks least informed; HKZ 2017 segmentation). Any retained weight should come from the system's OWN calibration-audit win rates for this line, not from the literature — the literature cannot justify heaviest-co-equal status.

Treat the proprietary buy-ratio sign as low-confidence by construction: midpoint executions dominate dark prints and defeat tick/quote-rule classification (Bartlett & McCrary). Consider requiring prints at/above the offer, or multi-day sign consistency, before counting a print as a 'buy', and track signing accuracy empirically where later price action resolves direction.

Fix the horizon claim: the only published dark-print informativeness is 15-120 MINUTES in less-liquid names via small algorithmic child orders (Nimalendran & Ray 2014); large negotiated crosses transmit LESS information. Days-weeks drift from large blocks has no published support.

Block prints may be lagging, not leading: upstairs literature shows price run-up to 4 weeks BEFORE the block as it is shopped (Keim & Madhavan 1996; Madhavan & Cheng 1997). Check pre-print run-up — a block printing after a multi-week rise is more consistent with accumulation ENDING than starting.

The conjunction with OI buildup helps but does not rescue the sign: Pan & Poteshman (2006 RFS) show option-volume predictability (>40bps next day, >1% next week for low vs high P/C) comes from NON-public signed open-buy data; public unsigned OI is far weaker. Keep the C28 distribution_flag (OI decrease w/ volume) logic — it is directionally consistent with this literature.

Herding-persistence cap: Sias autocorrelation is quarterly; multi-quarter persistence predicts long-run reversal concentrated in smaller, high-IO stocks (Dasgupta et al. 2011). Flag names where the accumulation thesis has persisted many weeks/quarters rather than scoring them higher.

A published, defensible alternative use of dark-share data: Thomas, Zhang & Zhu (2021 Mgmt Sci) — high dark-trading names under-react to earnings more (stronger PEAD). Conditioning post-earnings drift continuation on high dark share is literature-backed; 'DP block = direction' is not.

The one literature-backed bull case for the line: signed institutional order flow IS predictive at daily-weekly horizons (Hendershott, Livdan & Schürhoff 2015) — so the line's validity reduces entirely to whether the proprietary signing recovers true institutional direction from unsigned prints. That is an internal empirical question; run the per-line excess-winrate audit on the accumulation-hunter's +3 contributions before leaving it at +3.

key_citations.cite: Pan, J. & Poteshman, A.M. (2006), Review of Financial Studies 19(3), 871–908, "The Information in Option Volume for Future Stock Prices"
key_citations.finding: Verified from the full text (mit.edu/~junpan/volume.pdf). Critically for this system: when P/C ratios are built from PUBLICLY OBSERVABLE (Lee-Ready-signed) volume, signals 'are able to predict stock returns for only the next one or two trade days' and 'the stock prices subsequently reverse' — price pressure, not information; 'the publicly observed option volume has very little, if any, predictability.' Simultaneously SUPPORTS the system's −2 deduction when read as a continuation penalty: a RISING P/C z-score against a long candidate = informed put accretion = expected underperformance. key_citations.cite: Simon, D.P. & Wiggins, R.A. III (2001), Journal of Futures Markets 21(5), 447–462, "S&P futures returns and contrary sentiment indicators"
key_citations.finding: Verified (Wiley/ResearchGate). VIX, put-call ratio, and TRIN have statistically and economically significant CONTRARIAN forecasting power for S&P 500 futures returns over 10-, 20-, and 30-day horizons, Jan 1989–Jun 1999; out-of-sample trading simulations over the second half of the sample show profits enhanced by buying futures when fear indicators were HIGH; effect stronger the more extreme the sentiment. Note: this is the buy-the-fear side at INDEX level over multi-week horizons; related literature finds the sell-signal (greed/low-P/C) side much less reliable.

key_citations.cite: Ge, L., Lin, T.-C. & Pearson, N.D. (2016), Journal of Financial Economics 120(3), 601–622, "Why does the option to stock volume ratio predict stock returns?"
key_citations.finding: Verified. Using signed option volume: open-buy CALL purchases are the strongest predictor of (positive) future stock returns, followed by call sales closing purchased positions; predictability comes through the embedded-leverage channel; both synthetic-long and synthetic-short option trades contain information.

lanes.auditor_hypothesis: System usage: IV term-structure kink/backwardation at earnings expiry + back-month skew alignment decides BUY VOL vs SELL VOL pre-earnings. Verify: (a) Dubinsky-Johannes(-Kaeck-Seeger) earnings announcement jump risk priced in term structure; (b) implied earnings moves systematically exceed realized (sell event vol earns premium) vs Gao-Xing-Zhang evidence that buying pre-earnings straddles EARLY earns positive returns; (c) which side does the evidence favor and at what entry timing?

key_citations.cite: Dubinsky, Johannes, Kaeck & Seeger (2019), Review of Financial Studies 32(2), 646-687, "Option Pricing of Earnings Announcement Risks" (NOT Management Science; original WP: Dubinsky & Johannes 2006, SSRN 600593). Verified via open-access VU Amsterdam PDF, text extracted and read directly.
key_citations.finding: Deterministic earnings jumps make IV (1) rise nonlinearly as expiry approaches the EAD, (2) drop discontinuously after the announcement, and (3) produce a downward-sloping (backwardated/kinked) IV term structure pre-announcement — the paper's main estimator extracts the risk-neutral announcement vol Q_j from exactly that front-vs-back maturity differential, using ATM options only. Sample: actively traded US firms 2000-2015. Magnitudes: average option-implied earnings-day vol = 8.22% vs realized announcement-day vol = 7.42% — a premium of 80bps (56bps on close-to-open returns); stronger using medians/trimmed/standardized returns. ATM straddles opened at the close before the EAD and closed the next day average −8% (median −10%), bootstrap-significant. Incorporating the earnings jump cuts option pricing errors around EADs (e.g., AMZN short-dated errors 8.11%→3.69%); overall errors fall ~20%. Caveat found in their Table 4 subperiod stats: 2011-2015 Q-vol mean 6.78% vs P-vol(CC) 7.35% — the seller's premium appears to shrink/reverse in the latest subsample.
key_citations.relation: Supports (a) directly: announcement jump risk is priced in the term structure and the kink at the earnings expiry is the correct measurement object — the system's kink/backwardation detection mirrors the published estimator. Supports the sell-event-vol premium (b) on average, but only at the immediate pre-event entry, and only thinly (80bps of vol; −8% one-day straddle), with subsample instability.

key_citations.cite: Gao, Xing & Zhang (2018), Journal of Financial and Quantitative Analysis 53(6), 2587-2617, "Anticipating Uncertainty: Straddles around Earnings Announcements" (SSRN 2204549). Verified via Cambridge/RePEc abstracts.
key_citations.finding: Straddles on individual stocks generally earn significantly negative returns (~−3.15%/week baseline), BUT ATM straddles bought 3 days before an earnings announcement and held to the announcement date earn a highly significant +3.34% (sample 1996-2013) — capturing the pre-event IV run-up rather than the event itself (most announcements are AMC, so exit at announcement-date close precedes the news). Authors interpret this as investors underestimating uncertainty before announcements. Returns are larger for smaller firms, higher vol/kurtosis, more volatile past earnings surprises, and higher-transaction-cost names.
key_citations.relation: Supports buy-vol — but specifically at EARLY entry (T−3) with exit before the event. Contradicts a blanket "sell vol pre-earnings" rule: selling in the run-up window loses. Coexists with DJKS because the two papers trade different windows (run-up vs overnight event).

key_citations.relation: Supports and refines the sell-event-vol side with a recent (2025) cross-sectional discriminator: front-end curve SHAPE (concavity), not mere backwardation, identifies where the event premium is richest. Also qualifies the system: it uses front-curve concavity, not back-month skew, as the published shape signal.

Against \"sell event vol always\": (1) Gao-Xing-Zhang (JFQA 2018) — long ATM straddles T−3 to announcement date earn +3.34%, highly significant, i.e., vol is systematically UNDERpriced in the run-up window; (2) DJKS's own 2011-2015 subsample shows mean implied EAD vol (6.78%) BELOW realized close-to-close (7.35%) — the seller's premium reversed late-sample; (3) ORATS Feb-2026: realized moves > implied for a full season, straddle buyers +45% vs −2% 12-quarter baseline. nuances_for_plan: Citation hygiene: the canonical reference is Dubinsky, Johannes, Kaeck & Seeger, Review of Financial Studies 2019 (32(2):646-687), not Management Science; original is Dubinsky-Johannes 2006 SSRN WP 600593.

Kink/backwardation PRESENCE is mechanical before every earnings event (DJKS implication 3) and carries zero discriminating power by itself. The decision variable must be the kink MAGNITUDE: extract the implied earnings move Q_j from the front-vs-back IV differential (DJKS term-structure estimator) and compare it to the firm's historical realized EAD move distribution — sell only when implied >> historical realized, buy only when implied << historical realized.

Entry timing dominates direction. The published edges are window-specific: BUY VOL is supported entering ~T−3 (or earlier) and EXITING AT THE LAST PRE-ANNOUNCEMENT CLOSE (GXZ +3.34%); SELL VOL is supported only at the last pre-announcement close, closed the next session (DJKS −8% long-straddle, i.e., ~+8% to the seller gross). A single pre-earnings BUY/SELL verdict that holds through the event conflates two opposite-sign windows.

The seller's edge is thin and regime-unstable: +80bps of vol on average (56bps close-to-open), reversed in DJKS's 2011-2015 subsample, and inverted hard in the early-2026 season (ORATS: buyers +45%, realized > implied for weeks). Condition the SELL VOL default on a rolling universe-level implied-vs-realized EAD ratio (e.g., trailing 4-8 weeks) before allowing short-vol verdicts; in realized>implied regimes flip the prior to BUY or abstain.

The buy-early edge decayed post-publication and is cost-fragile: ~+1.2% gross 2011-2021, −9% after spreads (BSIC replication). Only emit BUY VOL (run-up) calls on liquid, tight-spread chains, and prefer the GXZ-favored cross-section (smaller, higher-vol, higher-kurtosis, volatile-surprise-history names) — while recognizing those overlap with the worst spreads.

"Back-month skew alignment" as a vol-direction decider has no direct published validation — keep it advisory (0 rubric points). The published shape signals are: front-end IV curve CONCAVITY/bimodality (Alexiou et al. RoF 2025 — flags bigger realized moves AND richer seller premium, i.e., favors defined-risk short structures, not naked shorts) and generic term-structure slope (Vasquez 2017 — but contaminated by the mechanical earnings inversion, so apply only ex-earnings).

Sell-side loss mode is tail risk, not average mispricing (META Feb-2022, NVDA May-2023: implied 12-14% vs realized ~24%). If the system emits SELL VOL pre-earnings, require defined-risk structures (iron fly/condor, capped calendars) and size to the tail, not to the 80bps average premium.

For the earnings-scout agent specifically: the existing front-end-IV-ratio + term-skew gates measure the right object (the DJKS kink), but the rubric should score the kink-implied move RELATIVE to the trailing realized EAD move (a ratio), not the kink in isolation; consider adding a concave-front-curve flag as an event-risk amplifier per RoF 2025.

Academic hedging-pressure effects are intraday and REVERT within days (Baltussen JFE 2021). The +3 weight (heaviest scored line) plus the internal trigger misfire means this line should be cut to advisory (0 points) pending internal cross-regime validation, mirroring the C15–C19 discipline.

If any dealer-positioning directional signal is retained, anchor it to the two mechanisms with peer-reviewed support: (a) cross-sectional net-gamma risk premium — high-NGE names underperform ~10%/yr (Soebhag JEF 2023), i.e., a slow cross-sectional tilt, not single-name flip timing; (b) intermediary-constraint shocks from DOTM SPX put net public buying predicting aggregate risk premia at ~monthly horizon (Chen-Joslin-Ni RFS 2019). Neither resembles a vanna-flip trigger; rebuild the lane around these or drop it.

If a vanna lane survives at all, restrict it to event-window IV-crush mechanics (post-FOMC/CPI/earnings vanna-charm flows) as an UNSCORED hypothesis with explicit internal backtest gates — that narrow setting is where practitioner claims are most plausible, but it has no published validation either.

Citation hygiene for the register: Barbon & Buraschi remains a working paper (not journal-published) — do not cite it as peer-reviewed; NPPW 2021 is RFS (not Management Science); Ni et al 2005 is JFE 78(1) 49–87. The dealer-gamma vol channel has genuinely strong publication support; the directional channel has none.

lanes.method: sector-rotation-persistence (multi-day persistent sector options-flow direction → multi-week sector rotation calls + single-name leaders, +1 conditional rubric point)
lanes.auditor_hypothesis: Multi-day persistent sector options-flow direction predicts multi-week sector rotation and single-name leadership, justified by (a) Moskowitz-Grinblatt 1999 industry momentum, (b) flow-induced price-pressure persistence (Coval-Stafford 2007, Lou 2012), and (c) options-flow-based sector rotation evidence.

key_citations.cite: Moskowitz & Grinblatt (1999), Journal of Finance 54(4), 1249-1290, "Do Industries Explain Momentum?"
key_citations.finding: Verified. Value-weighted long top-3 / short bottom-3 industry momentum earns ~0.43%/month (6-mo formation/6-mo hold); 0.40%/month (6,12); 0.53%/month (12,6). Crucially for this system, industry momentum is STRONGEST at the 1-month horizon — industry returns show significant positive 1-month autocorrelation while individual stocks reverse at 1 month — and persists up to ~12 months. Profits come mainly from the buy side and from the largest, most liquid stocks.
key_citations.relation: Supports the horizon mapping: short-lookback sector-level strength continuing for weeks is consistent with the 1-month industry-autocorrelation result. But the formation variable is past RETURNS, not options flow, and the short side is weaker — so it supports 'recent winning sectors keep winning ~1 month' rather than 'persistent options flow predicts rotation'.

key_citations.cite: Coval & Stafford (2007), Journal of Financial Economics 86(2), 479-512, "Asset Fire Sales (and Purchases) in Equity Markets"
key_citations.finding: Verified. Mutual fund flow-driven trading (1980-2004) creates significant price pressure in commonly held stocks; pressure is temporary and REVERSES (consistent with demand dislocation, not information); anticipated forced flows are predictable and front-runnable. Follow-up using their methodology (Mercado et al., European Accounting Review 2023) reports ~-1.39% abnormal return in the shock quarter on average and ~-18.1% (t-2 to t+3 months) in extreme cases, with ~15.0% reversal over the next 3 quarters and full reversion by ~20 months. Dyakov & Verbeek (2014, J. Banking & Finance, "Front-running of mutual fund fire-sales") find the front-running strategy earns ~0.5%/month alpha 1990-2010, and the pressure window COMPRESSED from ~1 month (1990s) to ~2 weeks (2000s).
key_citations.relation: Qualifies. Establishes that flow persistence has multi-week-to-quarter price impact (supports the horizon), but the pressure is non-informational and mean-reverting, and its exploitable window has shrunk toward 2 weeks — flow-persistence-based direction calls should expect eventual reversal, not fundamental continuation.

key_citations.cite: Lou (2012), Review of Financial Studies 25(12), 3457-3489, "A Flow-Based Explanation for Return Predictability"
key_citations.finding: Verified. Aggregated flow-induced trading (FIT) across mutual funds has significant temporary price impact; top-minus-bottom FIT decile spread ~22%. Expected FIT predicts returns positively in year 1 (E[FIT] +5.28% in the year after formation) and negatively thereafter (-5.67% over the subsequent two years); year-1 outperformance fully reversed by end of year 3. Flow effect partially explains stock price momentum; fund-alpha persistence spread 4.44%/yr.
key_citations.relation: Supports the continuation leg (predictable flow → months of continuation) and the idea that flow persistence is a real, measurable pressure channel; qualifies it because the continuation is uninformed price pressure that fully reverses — equity mutual fund flows at quarterly frequency, not multi-day options flow.

key_citations.cite: Pan & Poteshman (2006), Review of Financial Studies 19(3), 871-908, "The Information in Option Volume for Future Stock Prices"
key_citations.finding: Verified. Open-buy put-call ratios: low-PCR stocks outperform high-PCR stocks by >40 bps next DAY and >1% over the next WEEK; predictability stems from non-public information of option traders, decays over a couple of weeks, and does not reverse.
key_citations.relation: Supports single-name-leader selection from options flow at a days-to-2-weeks horizon; qualifies the system usage because the documented options-flow predictability horizon (1 day-2 weeks) is materially shorter than the system's multi-week rotation calls, and it is single-name, not sector-level.

key_citations.cite: Ge, Lin & Pearson (2016), Journal of Financial Economics 120(3), 601-622, "Why Does the Option to Stock Volume Ratio Predict Stock Returns?"
key_citations.finding: Verified. Using signed/open-close option volume: purchases of calls opening new positions are the strongest return predictor (then call sales closing bought positions); embedded leverage is the key channel for why option trading predicts returns.
key_citations.relation: Supports the system's OI-opening-gate design and using opening, directional options flow for single-name leaders; again single-name and short-horizon, not sector rotation.

key_citations.cite: Kaniel, Liu, et al. (2025), Journal of Financial Economics (article S0304405X25001618), "Why does options market information predict stock returns?"
key_citations.finding: Verified to exist (JFE 2025). Option order imbalances are transmitted to the stock market rapidly via market makers' delta-hedge trades; delta-weighted option flow forecasts subsequent stock order imbalance and SHORT-term returns; predictive power comes from ATM/ITM delta exposure, not OTM options.
key_citations.relation: Supports the mechanism (options flow moves underlying via hedging) with 2025 evidence, but the documented effect is short-term transmission — it does not validate multi-week sector-level continuation; also implies OTM-sweep-heavy flow is the weakest predictor leg.

key_citations.cite: Beber, Brandt & Kavajecz (2011), Review of Financial Studies 24(11), 3688-3730, "What Does Equity Sector Orderflow Tell Us about the Economy?"
key_citations.finding: Verified. The closest published analog to sector-flow rotation: aggregate cross-sector equity order flow rebalancing is consistent with sector rotation and predicts the evolution of the ECONOMY and future aggregate stock/bond market returns, beyond what relative sector prices reveal.
key_citations.relation: Qualifies. Confirms sector order flow contains information not in prices (validates watching flow, not just returns), but it is equity order flow (not options), and the predictability documented is macro/aggregate, not a cross-sectional long-winning-sector strategy.

key_citations.cite: Molchanov & Stangl (2024), International Journal of Finance & Economics 29(4), 4419-4442, "The Myth of Business Cycle Sector Rotation"
key_citations.finding: Verified. No evidence of systematic sector performance where conventional rotation wisdom expects it; at best modest outperformance that quickly vanishes after transaction costs and cycle-timing error; letting any industry's excess return predict other industries yields predictability not distinguishable from random chance.
key_citations.relation: Contradicts the strong form of multi-week sector rotation as a reliable edge (business-cycle/cross-industry version); does not directly test flow-based rotation, leaving the system's specific signal untested rather than refuted.

key_citations.cite: McLean & Pontiff (2016), Journal of Finance 71(1), "Does Academic Research Destroy Stock Return Predictability?"; Ehsani & Linnainmaa (2022, JF) and Arnott, Kalesnik & Linnainmaa et al. (2023, RFS) factor-momentum papers
key_citations.finding: Verified. Across 97 published predictors, returns are ~26% lower out-of-sample and ~58% lower post-publication. Factor momentum subsumes industry momentum in the 2023 RFS work (later papers partially rehabilitate industry momentum after fixing industry-linkage misspecification, so the subsumption is contested).
key_citations.relation: Qualifies. MG1999's 0.43%/month is an in-sample 1963-1995 number; expect roughly half or less today, and much of 'sector rotation' may be factor-tilt momentum in disguise rather than an independent sector signal.

lanes.counter_evidence: Strongest published counter-evidence: (1) Molchanov & Stangl (2024, IJFE) — generalized cross-industry/business-cycle sector rotation delivers predictability indistinguishable from chance after transaction costs and timing error; (2) Arnott-Kalesnik-Linnainmaa (2023, RFS) — factor momentum subsumes industry momentum, so sector signals may be repackaged factor exposure (contested by later replications); (3) horizon evidence cuts against the multi-week claim: documented options-flow predictability is 1 day to ~2 weeks (Pan-Poteshman 2006; 2025 JFE delta-hedge paper), and Dyakov-Verbeek (2014) show even flow-pressure front-running windows compressed to ~2 weeks in the modern market; (4) McLean-Pontiff (2016) — ~58% post-publication alpha decay across anomalies including momentum-family signals; (5) Eksi (2025, J. Financial Research) — part of single-stock options-signal predictability (IV spread/skew) is a measurement artifact from omitted borrow fees. Critically, NO published study directly tests multi-day persistent sector-level OPTIONS flow as a predictor of multi-week sector rotation — leg (c) of the hypothesis rests on analogy, not direct evidence.
nuances_for_plan: Keep the signal at +1 conditional/advisory and do not promote to a scored gate on the strength of the literature alone: the exact composite (sector-level options flow, multi-day persistence, multi-week horizon) has zero direct published validation — it is an inference stitched from adjacent literatures, so only the system's own calibration audits can validate it.

Horizon discipline: published options-flow predictability runs next-day to ~2 weeks (Pan-Poteshman >40bps/day, >1%/week; 2025 JFE delta-hedge channel is short-term). The multi-WEEK leg of a rotation call is carried by return-based industry momentum, not by the options flow itself — require sector relative-strength (price) confirmation before extending a flow-persistence call beyond ~2 weeks.

Asymmetry: MG1999 industry momentum profits come mainly from the BUY side and from large liquid names — long leaders in persistently-bought sectors is better supported than shorting persistently-sold sectors; weight short-side sector fades lower.

Expect reversal, not just decay: Coval-Stafford/Lou show flow-driven continuation is uninformed pressure that fully reverses (Lou: +5.28% year-1 reverses by year 3; fire-sale reversion over ~3-6 quarters). If sector flow looks like rebalancing/hedging pressure rather than informed opening flow, cap the holding horizon (≤1 quarter) and treat late-stage persistence as a contrarian setup, not a momentum one — the existing distribution_flag / OI-opening gates are the right kind of filter.

Single-name leader selection should privilege OPENING call buys and low open-buy put-call ratios (Ge-Lin-Pearson 2016; Pan-Poteshman 2006) and ATM/ITM delta-weighted flow over OTM sweeps (2025 JFE: predictive power is in ATM/ITM delta exposure, not OTM) — sector persistence as context, single-name opening flow as trigger.

Haircut any magnitude priors: MG1999's 0.43%/month is pre-publication, 1963-1995; McLean-Pontiff implies ~50%+ decay, and flow-pressure windows have compressed from ~1 month to ~2 weeks since the 1990s (Dyakov-Verbeek). Do not anchor sizing or win-rate priors on the 1999 magnitudes.

Beware factor-tilt confounds: 2023 RFS evidence that factor momentum subsumes industry momentum means a persistent 'sector' flow may just be a beta/duration/factor move (e.g., tech flow = long-duration growth factor). When the rotation call coincides with an obvious macro factor move, attribute it to the factor in the report rather than crediting sector-flow alpha.

Beber-Brandt-Kavajecz legitimizes the general design (sector order flow contains information beyond prices) but its payoff was macro/aggregate prediction — consider using persistent cross-sector flow rotation also as a regime/risk input (e.g., flow into defensives as a risk-off flag) where the evidence is stronger, not only as a cross-sectional winner-picker.

lanes.auditor_hypothesis: System usage: fresh long-dated (DTE>180) OI builds + near-to-far rolls + slow premium accretion over 30-90d = informed multi-quarter conviction (LEAP book; +2 weekly rolls scoring line). Verify (a) tenor concentration of informed traders, (b) whether long-dated flow is dominated by hedging/overwriting/financing, (c) any published evidence FOR long-dated flow informativeness.

key_citations.cite: Pan & Poteshman (2006), Review of Financial Studies 19(3):871-908, "The Information in Option Volume for Future Stock Prices" (https://academic.oup.com/rfs/article-abstract/19/3/871/1646711; https://www.mit.edu/~junpan/volume.pdf)
key_citations.finding: Open-buy put-call ratios predict returns: low-P/C stocks outperform high-P/C by >40 bps next day and >1% over the next week (risk-adjusted). Predictive power strongest for deep-OTM options and full-service-customer flow; attributed to non-public information.
key_citations.relation: Qualifies the system usage: the canonical informed-flow signal lives in short-dated, high-leverage, freshly opened positions — not LEAPs. It validates the 'opening flow' construct the agent uses, but at the opposite end of the tenor curve.

key_citations.cite: Augustin, Brenner & Subrahmanyam (2019), Management Science 65(12), "Informed Options Trading Prior to Takeover Announcements: Insider Trading?" (https://pubsonline.informs.org/doi/10.1287/mnsc.2018.3122)
key_citations.finding: ~25% of takeover targets show positive abnormal option volume pre-announcement, concentrated in SHORT-dated, out-of-the-money calls (leverage maximization); over half of the abnormal activity is not explained by rumors, insiders' filings, or deal predictability.
key_citations.relation: Contradicts the default reading that big fresh long-dated builds are the preferred informed vehicle: when informed traders demonstrably act (M&A), they go short-dated OTM.

key_citations.cite: Augustin, Brenner, Grass, Orłowski & Subrahmanyam (2023), Journal of Financial Markets, "Informed Options Strategies before Corporate Events" (https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S1386418122000568; SSRN 2848989)
key_citations.finding: Leverage-ranking framework across 12 corporate-event categories: with precise timing signals, informed investors maximize leverage in short-maturity options just before the event; GREATER EVENT-DATE UNCERTAINTY pushes informed investors into LONGER-maturity options. Option tenor choice responds to timing precision of private information.
key_citations.relation: The strongest published (conditional) support for the system usage: long-tenor informed positioning is rational when the catalyst date is uncertain — i.e., exactly the multi-quarter-thesis case the LEAP radar targets. But 'longer maturity' in their setting means months around events, not a validated DTE>180 OI-build alpha.

key_citations.cite: Lakonishok, Lee, Pearson & Poteshman (2007), Review of Financial Studies 20(3):813-857, "Option Market Activity" (https://academic.oup.com/rfs/article-abstract/20/3/813/1563935)
key_citations.finding: Account-level CBOE data: a large percentage of call writing is covered-call positions; the average non-market-maker option position is net SHORT, consistent with income generation (covered calls, cash-secured puts) rather than directional information.
key_citations.relation: Supports hypothesis (b): the bulk of customer option positioning — especially the standing OI the agent reads — is overwriting/income, not conviction. Directly validates the agent's hard rejection of COVERED_CALL / HEDGED_LONG scenarios as a necessary (not sufficient) filter.

key_citations.cite: Garleanu, Pedersen & Poteshman (2009), Review of Financial Studies 22(10):4259-4299, "Demand-Based Option Pricing" (https://academic.oup.com/rfs/article-abstract/22/10/4259/1590158)
key_citations.finding: End users are net long index options — especially OTM puts (portfolio hedging); demand pressure raises prices proportionally to unhedgeable risk, explaining the smirk and single-stock option price patterns.
key_citations.relation: Supports (b): persistent long-dated demand is heavily hedging-driven and moves PRICES via dealer risk-bearing — so premium accretion can reflect demand pressure/hedging, not information.

key_citations.cite: Clements, Kalesnik & Linnainmaa (2017 SSRN 3043461 "Informed Traders, Long-Dated Options, and the Cross Section of Stock Returns"; revised Dec 2019 as "Why do option prices predict stock returns?", AEA 2020 preliminary, https://www.aeaweb.org/conference/2020/preliminary/paper/kGGBN5Q2)
key_citations.finding: Original 2017 version: long-dated option prices contain essentially all cross-sectional return-relevant information, framed as informed traders with slow-arriving information choosing long maturities. The authors' own 2019 revision RETRACTS that interpretation: long-dated puts capitalize expected shorting costs over the option's life. Fama-MacBeth t-stat on IV spread falls from -6.01 to -2.43 once borrow costs are controlled; option prices do NOT predict returns among easy-to-borrow stocks; top-decile expensive-put names carry >5%/yr lending fees (extremes >50%/yr with 47% IV spreads); single-day quote measures inflate predictability (t = -10.67 end-of-month vs -6.19 week-averaged) via liquidity noise in thinly traded long-dated options.
key_citations.relation: The pivotal citation. The ONLY prominent paper supporting long-dated informativeness was rewritten by its own authors into a securities-lending/financing story — converting the best pro-evidence into counter-evidence for the system's informed-conviction interpretation.

key_citations.cite: Muravyev, Pearson & Pollet (2025), Journal of Financial Economics 172:104153, "Why does options market information predict stock returns?" (https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0304405X25001618)
key_citations.finding: Published confirmation of the borrow-fee mechanism: derives a formula tying the put-call implied-volatility spread to the stock borrow fee; return predictability from IV spread and skew falls by AT LEAST two-thirds when high-borrow-fee stocks are excluded.
key_citations.relation: Contradicts informed-trading readings of long-dated price/positioning signals: most of what option-implied measures 'know' about future returns is the financing condition of the stock, not directional conviction.

key_citations.cite: Fodor, Krieger & Doran (2011), Financial Markets and Portfolio Management 25:265-280, "Do option open-interest changes foreshadow future equity returns?" (https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s11408-011-0164-z)
key_citations.finding: Large increases in call OI are followed by significantly higher equity returns; rising put OI precedes weaker returns but the put-side effect attenuates considerably with controls; call/put OI-change ratio predicts returns over the FOLLOWING WEEK.
key_citations.relation: Partial support for the 'fresh OI build' construct — but it is aggregate (not tenor-stratified), one-week horizon (not multi-quarter), and the put leg is fragile. No test of DTE>180 builds exists.

key_citations.cite: Bryzgalova, Pavlova & Sikorskaya (2023), Journal of Finance 78(6):3465-3514, "Retail Trading in Options and the Rise of the Big Three Wholesalers" (https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/jofi.13285)
key_citations.finding: Documents the post-2019 surge of retail options trading via PFOF wholesalers (~90% of PFOF from three firms); retail prefers cheap, SHORT-dated weekly options (average relative bid-ask spread 12.6%) and loses money on average.
key_citations.relation: Qualifies: modern option volume is increasingly short-dated and retail-noise-heavy, so long-dated books are comparatively institutional — but the institutional residue in long tenors is precisely where overwriting/hedging/financing concentrates (Lakonishok 2007; van Binsbergen 2022).

key_citations.cite: van Binsbergen, Diamond & Grotteria (2022), Journal of Financial Economics 143(1), "Risk-Free Interest Rates" (https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0304405X21002786; NBER w26138)
key_citations.finding: Recovers risk-free rates from index option box spreads at maturities up to 3 YEARS at minutely frequency (Treasury convenience yield ~40 bps, quadrupling in crises) — demonstrating that long-dated options markets function at scale as financing/rates venues.
key_citations.relation: Supports (b): a material share of long-dated option volume/OI exists for financing (boxes, conversions/reversals, synthetic borrow), which an OI/premium-accretion scanner can misread as directional conviction.

key_citations.cite: Evans, Geczy, Musto & Reed (2009), Review of Financial Studies 22(5):1955-1980, "Failure Is an Option: Impediments to Short Selling and Options Prices" (https://academic.oup.com/rfs/article-abstract/22/5/1955/1592920)
key_citations.finding: Options market makers in hard-to-borrow names often fail to deliver rather than borrow; short-sale impediments (reverse conversions etc.) systematically distort option prices and generate non-informational option activity in HTB names.
key_citations.relation: Supports (b): in high short-interest / hard-to-borrow names, long-dated option positioning and pricing are polluted by short-sale-constraint workarounds — a specific false-positive channel for the LEAP radar.

lanes.counter_evidence: Strongest published counter-evidence: (1) Muravyev, Pearson & Pollet (JFE 2025, 172:104153) — option-implied predictability (IV spread/skew) is ≥2/3 attributable to stock borrow fees, not informed directional flow; (2) Clements, Kalesnik & Linnainmaa — the original 2017 working paper that claimed "the prices of long-dated options contain all the information relevant for predicting returns" was revised (Dec 2019) by its own authors into a shorting-cost-capitalization story (Fama-MacBeth t falls -6.01 → -2.43 with borrow-fee controls; zero predictability among easy-to-borrow stocks; information concentrates in long-dated quotes mechanically because longer maturity capitalizes more expected borrow cost, and long-dated contracts are 'typically very thinly traded'); (3) Lakonishok et al. (RFS 2007) — standing non-market-maker open interest is dominated by covered-call/income writing, i.e., the default interpretation of a long-dated OI build should be overwriting/hedging/financing, not conviction. No published study directly validates DTE>180 OI builds, near→far rolls, or 30-90d premium accretion as multi-quarter alpha.
nuances_for_plan: Keep the LEAP lane advisory/low-weight: there is NO published validation of DTE>180 OI builds, near-to-far rolls, or 30-90d premium accretion as a return signal at any horizon; the '+2 weekly rolls' scoring line is externally unsupported and should stay subject to internal /calibration-audit evidence before carrying rubric points.

The agent's hard rejection of HEDGED_LONG and COVERED_CALL scenarios is exactly the right filter per Lakonishok et al. (2007) — most standing customer OI is income/hedging. Extend it to also flag collar structures (long put + short call vs stock) and conversion/reversal/box-like financing structures, which Lakonishok's scenario taxonomy and the conviction-matrix may not separate.

Add a borrow-fee / short-interest disqualifier: in high short-interest or hard-to-borrow names, long-dated put-side OI, elevated put IV, and put-call 'skew' are largely capitalized financing costs (Muravyev-Pearson-Pollet 2025; Clements et al. 2019; Evans et al. 2009), not directional information. The existing fz short-interest lane is the natural cross-check — treat put-side LEAP reads in high-SI names as financing noise by default.

Deep-ITM long-dated call premium accretion in high-dividend names is dividend/financing arbitrage, not conviction — consistent with the project's existing NEE dividend-capture blind-spot memory; a parity/ex-div check should gate cum-premium-flow before it counts toward the slow-accretion signature.

Condition the LEAP thesis on catalyst-timing uncertainty: the only published support for informed long-tenor positioning (Augustin et al., JFM 2023) is that informed traders extend maturity when the event DATE is uncertain. Require the thesis line to name a multi-quarter catalyst class with uncertain timing (regulatory decision, product cycle, restructuring); absent one, the prior should default to hedging/financing/overwriting.

Expect a low base rate of informed flow in long tenors: leverage preference (Black 1975; Pan-Poteshman 2006; Augustin et al. 2019) concentrates informed directional trading in short-dated OTM contracts. The 6-of-9 gate stack is appropriately strict — do not loosen it to increase candidate counts.

Long-dated contracts are thinly traded, so single-day quote/flow snapshots are noisy and overstate signal (Clements et al.: end-of-month vs week-averaged IV spread t = -10.67 vs -6.19 purely from liquidity noise). Prefer multi-day averaged measures (the 30/90d cumulative-premium-flow gate is the right shape) and require block-print/dark-pool corroboration rather than quote-derived metrics alone.

Roll-direction heuristics (balance ratio >0.7 = thesis intact; far-to-near = de-risking) have no literature support either way — keep them descriptive/diagnostic rather than scored, and note that position-roll detections can also be market-maker calendar-spread activity.

Horizon hygiene is already correct and should be preserved: even genuinely informed long-dated positioning embeds slow-arriving information — it is not a next-session signal and must never leak into next-session conviction scoring.

key_citations.finding: Put-call ratios built ONLY from buyer-initiated open-new-position volume predict returns: low-P/C stocks outperform high-P/C stocks by >40bps next day, >1% next week (risk-adjusted). Predictability is two-sided (high P/C predicts low returns AND low P/C predicts high returns), driven by non-public information; strongest from full-service-broker customers, with firm proprietary trader volume NOT informative; no informed trading found in index options; publicly observable signals predict only 1-2 days then reverse.

Their firm-prop result also cautions that the largest/most institutional flow was the LEAST informative class.

key_citations.cite: Cremers & Weinbaum, 2010, Journal of Financial and Quantitative Analysis 45:335-367, "Deviations from Put-Call Parity and Stock Return Predictability"
key_citations.finding: Stocks with relatively expensive calls outperform stocks with relatively expensive puts by ~50bps/week; abnormal performance exists on BOTH legs (positive for expensive-call stocks, negative for expensive-put stocks). Authors explicitly argued the effect is NOT explained by short-sale constraints (checked rebate rates).

Confirms bearish option-price information predicts downside (expensive-put leg is negative), but it is a price-based (IV-spread) signal, not trade-level whale flow, the effect is two-sided, and CW themselves rejected the short-sale-constraint channel the system invokes — a channel later resurrected by Muravyev-Pearson-Pollet 2025 with better borrow-fee data.

key_citations.cite: Xing, Zhang & Zhao, 2010, Journal of Financial and Quantitative Analysis 45:641-662, "What Does the Individual Option Volatility Smirk Tell Us About Future Equity Returns?"
key_citations.finding: Stocks with the steepest OTM-put volatility smirks underperform flattest-smirk stocks by 10.9%/year risk-adjusted; predictability persists up to ~6 months; interpreted as informed traders with negative news preferring OTM puts, equity market slow to incorporate.
key_citations.relation: Supports the bearish-puts-as-informed-venue premise — the strongest classical evidence that negative information shows up in puts specifically. Caveat: it is a slow (weeks-months) price-based signal, not a next-session trade-size signal, and MPP 2025 shows much of it proxies borrow fees.

key_citations.cite: Ofek, Richardson & Whitelaw, 2004, Journal of Financial Economics 74:305-342, "Limited Arbitrage and Short Sales Restrictions: Evidence from the Options Markets"
key_citations.finding: Put-call parity violations are asymmetric in the direction of short-sale constraints, strongly related to the rebate-rate spread, survive transaction costs, and both violation size and shorting cost significantly predict future (negative) stock returns.
key_citations.relation: Supports the claimed channel (d): when shorting stock is costly, bearish information migrates to options and the bearish side carries predictive content. Implies the put-whale edge should concentrate in hard-to-borrow names rather than apply uniformly.

key_citations.cite: Chakravarty, Gulen & Mayhew, 2004, Journal of Finance 59:1235-1257, "Informed Trading in Stock and Option Markets"
key_citations.finding: Using Hasbrouck information shares on 60 firms over 5 years, the option market contributes ~17% of price discovery on average (12-23% range), higher for higher-leverage (OTM) options and related to relative volumes/spreads.
key_citations.relation: Supports the general premise that options host informed trading and that leverage (OTM, short-dated) is where it concentrates. Does not speak to single-leg vs multi-leg or to put-vs-call asymmetry — citing it for "single-leg price discovery" overstates it; the paper predates leg-level decompositions.

key_citations.cite: Johnson & So, 2012, Journal of Financial Economics 106:262-286, "The Option to Stock Volume Ratio and Future Returns"
key_citations.finding: Theory + empirics: equity short-sale costs make options the preferred venue for negative news, generating a NEGATIVE relation between O/S and future returns; lowest-O/S decile outperforms highest by 0.34%/week (~19.3% annualized); signal stronger when short-sale costs are high.
key_citations.relation: This is the correct citation for the bearish-asymmetry claim the system attributes to Pan-Poteshman — directly supports 'bearish option signals stronger than bullish' via the short-sale-cost channel.

key_citations.cite: Ge, Lin & Pearson, 2016, Journal of Financial Economics 120:601-622, "Why Does the Option to Stock Volume Ratio Predict Stock Returns?"
key_citations.finding: Using ISE signed open/close volume: NO evidence that trades creating synthetic short exposure contain more information than synthetic long trades; OPENING CALL PURCHASES are the strongest return predictor (followed by closing call sales); embedded leverage, not short-sale avoidance, is the dominant channel.
key_citations.relation: Contradicts the put-side-dominant asymmetry and the 'calls are beta' claim at the level of signed opening volume — the best leg-level dataset found bullish opening flow MORE informative. Forces the internal call-NO_GO to be read as regime-/benchmark-specific, not structural.

key_citations.cite: Muravyev, Pearson & Pollet, 2025, Journal of Financial Economics 172, "Why Does Options Market Information Predict Stock Returns?"
key_citations.finding: The CW volatility spread and XZZ skew predict returns largely because they proxy for the stock borrow fee paid by short sellers; return predictability from IV spread and skew falls by at least two-thirds when high-borrow-fee stocks are excluded.
key_citations.relation: Qualifies (b) and (c) heavily while supporting channel (d): the classical bearish price-signal alpha is concentrated in hard-to-borrow stocks and is mostly a constraint premium, not detectable informed flow. Implies the put-whale edge should be conditioned on borrow-cost/short-interest and expected to be weak in easy-to-borrow large caps.

key_citations.cite: Strong (Cuyler Strong), forthcoming/2024-25, Journal of Portfolio Management, "The Information Content of Unusual Option Activity"
key_citations.finding: Decade of UOA data: large option trades are IN GENERAL NOT predictive of returns; significant positive abnormal returns only for the subset of large trades that are close to expiration and not yet at the strike; author's chair cautions popularization may be eroding the edge.
key_citations.relation: Contradicts the blanket '$500K+ whale = informed' premise but supports the system's specific conditioning (DTE≤30, away-from-strike/OTM): the predictive UOA subset matches the system's filter set, the unconditional whale signal does not.

key_citations.cite: Muravyev, 2016, Journal of Finance 71(2):673-708, "Order Flow and Expected Option Returns"
key_citations.finding: Decomposing option trade price impact: the inventory-risk component is larger than the asymmetric-information component; option order imbalances mostly move option prices through market-maker inventory, with imbalance effects ~5x larger than previously attributed to inventory.
key_citations.relation: Qualifies: most option order flow — including large prints — is inventory/hedging, not information, so unconditional flow-following has no edge; only sharply conditioned subsets (opening, short-dated, single-name) plausibly carry signal.

key_citations.cite: Augustin, Brenner & Subrahmanyam, 2019, Management Science 65(12):5697-5720, "Informed Options Trading Prior to Takeover Announcements: Insider Trading?"
key_citations.finding: In 1,859 U.S. takeovers (1996-2012), ~25% show abnormal pre-announcement option volume, concentrated in SHORT-DATED, OUT-OF-THE-MONEY options (calls, for targets); over half of abnormal activity not explained by speculation, rumors, or insider filings.
key_citations.relation: Supports the DTE≤30 + OTM conditioning as where informed traders concentrate — but note the canonical event-driven informed flow here is on the CALL side, again undermining a universal put-only asymmetry.

key_citations.cite: Bryzgalova, Pavlova & Sikorskaya, 2023, Journal of Finance 78(6):3465-3514, "Retail Trading in Options and the Rise of the Big Three Wholesalers"
key_citations.finding: 2019-2021 transaction flags: retail dominates small single-leg trades routed to three wholesalers (~90% of PFOF); retail prefers cheap short-dated weeklies (avg 12.6% relative spread) and loses money on average.
key_citations.relation: Qualifies the modern data environment: post-2020 single-leg short-dated flow is heavily retail and noise-laden; the $500K size floor is what keeps the system's signal out of this retail pool, so the size filter is load-bearing for excluding uninformed flow even though size alone does not certify informed flow.

lanes.counter_evidence: Strongest counter-evidence to the specific put-side asymmetry: Ge, Lin & Pearson (2016, JFE 120:601-622) — using the best available signed open/close ISE data, they find NO evidence that synthetic-short (bearish) option trades are more informative than synthetic-long trades, and that opening CALL purchases are the single strongest stock-return predictor; embedded leverage, not short-sale avoidance, drives O/S predictability. Secondary: Strong (J. Portfolio Management, forthcoming) finds large option trades are in general NOT predictive (only the near-expiry, not-yet-at-strike subset is); Pan-Poteshman (2006) themselves found firm proprietary (large institutional) volume uninformative; Muravyev (2016, JF) shows option order-flow price impact is mostly market-maker inventory rather than information; and Muravyev-Pearson-Pollet (2025, JFE) shows the classical bearish price signals (CW spread, XZZ skew) lose ≥2/3 of their predictability once high-borrow-fee stocks are excluded — i.e., bearish option-signal alpha is largely a hard-to-borrow phenomenon, not a general whale-flow edge.
nuances_for_plan: Re-attribute the asymmetry citation: Pan-Poteshman 2006 documents a two-sided open-buy P/C signal (~40bps next day, both legs), not put-side dominance. The correct external anchors for bearish-stronger are Johnson-So 2012 (short-sale-cost channel, 0.34%/week) and Xing-Zhang-Zhao 2010 (OTM-put venue). C19 documentation should cite Johnson-So, not Pan-Poteshman, for claim (a).

Condition the put-whale edge on short-sale-constraint proxies. Muravyev-Pearson-Pollet (JFE 2025) shows bearish option-signal predictability collapses by >=2/3 outside high-borrow-fee stocks. The fz CLI short-interest/float lane is the right conditioning variable: expect the C19 edge to concentrate in high short-interest / hard-to-borrow names and be weak on easy-to-borrow megacaps. Worth adding short-interest as a split in the 60-day cross-regime validation.

Do not generalize 'calls are beta' beyond the bull-regime benchmark. Ge-Lin-Pearson 2016 found opening call buys the STRONGEST predictor in absolute terms; the internal -9.7pp call result is plausibly an artifact of benchmarking high-beta call activity against SPY in a rising tape. Keep the call NO_GO regime-tagged and re-test calls explicitly in bear/neutral regimes before hard-coding the asymmetry.

Size alone is not informativeness — the conditioning stack is load-bearing. Pan-Poteshman found firm-prop (large) flow uninformative and Strong (JPM) finds large trades generally non-predictive EXCEPT near-expiry, not-yet-at-strike subsets. The system's DTE<=30 + opening (size/OI>=2) + ask-side filters match the predictive subset; consider adding an explicit moneyness/distance-to-strike filter (OTM or near-strike-but-not-through), which both Strong and Augustin et al. 2019 identify as where informed trades sit.

Horizon discipline: literature predictability from publicly observable option signals lasts ~1-2 days and partially reverses (Pan-Poteshman); vendor-distributed UW flow is effectively public. Next-session usage is correctly matched — do not extend C19 holding periods to multi-week without separate validation, and expect reversal risk if entry is delayed a session.

Treat the internal magnitude (+22-26pp next-session excess, WR 0.60-0.64) as far above any published analog — academic long-short option-flow signals run ~40bps/day on decile portfolios. With n=295 in a single regime, assume substantial shrinkage (post-publication factor decay alone averages ~30-58% in McLean-Pontiff-style studies, and UOA popularization is noted as eroding the edge); keep C19 at 0 rubric points until the cross-regime audit clears it.

Keep the universe restricted to single-name common stock: Pan-Poteshman found NO informed trading in index options, so the existing common-stock-only filter is externally validated; do not extend C19 to ETF/index puts where flow is dominated by hedging (Muravyev 2016 inventory result).

The size/OI<0.5 'closing anti-signal' is direction-ambiguous, not pure noise: Ge-Lin-Pearson found closing call sales were the second-strongest (negative-side) predictor, i.e., closing trades can carry information. Safe to use as a disqualifier for the opening-print edge, unsafe to use as a contrarian signal.

lanes.method: zerodte-premium-selling (open-entry 0DTE short-straddle/iron-condor on SPX/SPY/QQQ, VIX-tercile sizing, GEX-derived wings, intraday-only / never-overnight)
