Internal validation: +0.30-0.39%/day, 90-95% win, n=43, tail unsampled.

key_citations.cite: Carr, P. & Wu, L. (2009), Review of Financial Studies 22(3):1311-1341, "Variance Risk Premiums"
key_citations.finding: Verified against the published PDF (tables extracted directly). SPX sample Jan-1996 to Feb-2003 (1,779 obs): mean variance risk premium RP = 100×(RV−SW) = −2.279 (t = −7.19, Newey-West 30 lags); mean log VRP ln(RV/SW) = −0.594 (t = −9.48) — i.e., long variance swaps lose >50% continuously-compounded per 30-day holding period. Shorting SPX/DJX variance swaps yields raw annualized information ratios > 3 (lower after serial-dependence adjustment but still above equity portfolios). Negative beta and FF3 factors cannot explain it (alphas remain strongly negative).
key_citations.relation: Supports existence/robustness of a large index VRP — but at ~30-day horizon, not same-day. It legitimizes the strategy family, not the system's specific intraday 0DTE magnitude claim.

key_citations.cite: Bollerslev, T., Tauchen, G. & Zhou, H. (2009), Review of Financial Studies 22(11):4463-4492, "Expected Stock Returns and Variance Risk Premia"
key_citations.finding: Verified against the published PDF: Jan-1990–Dec-2007, mean implied variance 33.23 vs realized 14.93 (monthly, percentage-squared) → mean VRP (IV−RV) = 18.30, i.e., implied ≈ 2.2× realized. VRP predicts market returns with peak at quarterly horizon: t = 2.86, adj-R² = 6.82% (the often-quoted ">15% quarterly R²" is the earlier 1990-2005 working-paper sample; published 1990-2007 value is 6.82%).
key_citations.relation: Supports a persistent, time-varying VRP and supports state-dependent sizing (premium is conditional, not constant). Again 30-day, not 0DTE-horizon, evidence.

key_citations.cite: Vilkov, G. (2024, updated through Feb-2026), SSRN 4641356, "0DTE Trading Rules" (sample 09/2016–01/2026, Cboe 30-min SPXW bars + NBBO)
key_citations.finding: A positive 0DTE VRP exists but is economically tiny: median realized VRP from 10:00 ET to expiry ≈ 0.0011% of underlying; even zero-realized-variance max payoff ≈ 0.20% of spot. Unconditional short-premium templates: short strangles win in ≥75% of observations but mean PnL ≈ 0; iron condors gross Sharpe 0.77 → NET Sharpe −0.20 after half-spread + 0.5bp costs. Net PnL distributions are 'dominated by tail risk rather than stable mean carry'; ES(1%) = 0.58%–1.58% of underlying. Results qualitatively unchanged across entry times (prior close, 10:00, 13:00, 15:00 ET). Only conditional out-of-sample rules survive: put ratio spreads gross SR 1.18 / net 0.93; top-3 equal-weight basket gross 1.12 / net 0.82 — 'selective timing opportunities rather than a broad unconditional edge.'
key_citations.relation: Qualifies strongly / partially contradicts. High win rate matches the system's 90-95% observation, but published mean carry for unconditional open-entry short straddles/condors is ~zero gross and negative net — the claimed +0.30-0.39%/day cannot come from the unconditional same-day VRP (median ~0.1bp of spot). Supports the conditioning idea (VIX/GEX states) but not the structure choice or the expectancy claim.

key_citations.cite: Beckmeyer, H., Branger, N. & Gayda, L. (2023, SSRN 4404704), "Retail Traders Love 0DTE Options... But Should They?"
key_citations.finding: ~75%+ of retail S&P 500 option trades are 0DTE; retail are NET BUYERS of 0DTE. Cumulative retail losses > $70M over ~2.5 years (Feb-2021–Sep-2023 in the updated draft), of which > $50M is transaction costs paid to market makers; gross (pre-cost) retail PnL ≈ −$20M by end of sample. Press summaries quote $240k–$356k/day average retail losses depending on draft/period. Market makers carry the net-short inventory and profit primarily via spread capture.
key_citations.relation: Qualifies. Answers 'who wins/loses': the seller side's counterpart profit is mostly market-maker spread revenue, not harvestable VRP carry — retail's GROSS loss (≈$20M of $70M) is the upper bound of what a non-MM premium seller competes for. A retail-account premium seller pays the same spreads that drive 71% of documented losses.

key_citations.cite: Dim, C., Eraker, B. & Vilkov, G. (2024), SSRN 4692190, "0DTEs: Trading, Gamma Risk and Volatility Propagation"; and Adams, Dim, Eraker, Fontaine, Ornthanalai & Vilkov (2025), SSRN 5641974, "Do S&P500 Options Increase Market Volatility? Evidence from 0DTEs"
key_citations.finding: 0DTE options carry the largest (relative) volatility risk premium of any maturity. Market-maker net gamma from 0DTE/short-dated OI is on average positive and NEGATIVELY related to future intraday realized volatility (positive gamma → vol damping, stronger intraday reversal); no destabilizing propagation to overnight vol found. Cboe data (Mandy Xu): 0DTE ≈ 62% of SPX volume by Aug-2025, flow balanced between buys/sells, ~53% retail, no one-sided positioning.
key_citations.relation: Supports two system elements: (1) a real, relatively large 0DTE VRP exists (in vol-unit terms — tiny in absolute %-of-spot per day); (2) GEX-based range/wing logic has published backing as an intraday realized-vol conditioner. Does not establish positive net expectancy for unconditional short premium.

key_citations.cite: Muravyev, D. & Ni, X. (2020), Journal of Financial Economics 136(1):219-238, "Why Do Option Returns Change Sign from Day to Night?"
key_citations.finding: Delta-hedged S&P 500 option (and straddle) returns decompose as: INTRADAY +0.22%/day (t = 2.3) for longs, OVERNIGHT −0.93% (t = −12.1); total −0.7%/day. Pattern holds across maturities/moneyness and equity options. Explanation: option prices fail to reflect that volatility is much higher intraday than overnight.
key_citations.relation: CONTRADICTS the open-entry/intraday-only premise as a general principle: option SELLERS earn the premium overnight and have ~negative expected returns intraday. For fixed-maturity options, selling at open and closing at the bell is the wrong half of the day. (For 0DTE the overnight half is mechanically inaccessible — which means 0DTE selling forgoes the documented profitable component.)

key_citations.cite: Papagelis, L. & Dotsis, G. (2025), Journal of Futures Markets 45(7):752-770, "The Variance Risk Premium Over Trading and Nontrading Periods"
key_citations.finding: Decomposes model-free VRP (Carr-Wu RV−IV convention) into overnight and intraday components across US/Europe/Asia indices: overnight VRP significantly NEGATIVE (sellers profit overnight); intraday VRP POSITIVE and often insignificant (realized ≥ implied during trading hours — sellers roughly break even or lose gross). The overall negative VRP documented in prior studies is largely driven by the overnight component; 'going long volatility at the open and closing at the close tends to be profitable on most days, except Fridays.'
key_citations.relation: CONTRADICTS the evidential basis of the never-overnight rule: the published VRP split runs opposite to the system's framing. The intraday window is the thin/zero part of the premium, not the safe part. The 0DTE-specific tiny-positive median (Vilkov) is the system's best remaining support.

lanes.counter_evidence: Three-layer stack: (1) Muravyev-Ni (JFE 2020): straddle returns +0.22%/day intraday vs −0.93% overnight — premium selling earns overnight, loses intraday; (2) Papagelis-Dotsis (JFM 2025): the negative index VRP is largely an overnight phenomenon; intraday VRP is positive/insignificant, and long-vol-at-open/close-at-bell is profitable most days — directly the opposite trade to the system's; (3) Vilkov (SSRN 4641356, 09/2016–01/2026): unconditional open- or 10:00-entry 0DTE short straddles/strangles have ~zero mean gross PnL, iron condors NET Sharpe −0.20 after half-spread + 0.5bp, PnL tail-dominated with ES(1%) of 0.58-1.58% of underlying — one tail day erases roughly 2-5 weeks of the system's claimed +0.30-0.39%/day carry, and n=43 (≈2 months, single low-vol regime) has expected tail-day count < 1, so the internal 90-95% win / positive-mean result is exactly what the published tail-dominated distribution generates before the tail is sampled. Practitioner tail datapoint: Aug 5, 2024 (VIX 65 intraday) — forced liquidations of short-vol books with margin-call amplification.
nuances_for_plan: Keep this lane permanently advisory unless promoted on EXPECTANCY-WITH-TAIL-PRIOR, never on win rate: with published ES(1%) of 0.58-1.58% of underlying, score the strategy by injecting one synthetic ES-size loss per ~100 trades; n=43 with 0 tail days cannot distinguish +0.30%/day from a negative true mean.

Re-express the internal +0.30-0.39%/day on an explicit basis (premium collected vs underlying notional vs margin). If it is %-of-underlying it exceeds the entire published same-day premium pool (median realized 0DTE VRP ~0.1bp of spot; max zero-vol payoff ~0.20% of spot) and the backtest window is regime luck; if %-of-premium/margin, restate so audits compare like-for-like with Vilkov's numbers.

Net-of-cost is the binding test: Vilkov's unconditional iron condor flips from +0.77 gross to −0.20 net Sharpe at half-spread + 0.5bp. Log actual fill-vs-mid on every 0DTE leg and apply that haircut in the lane's PnL accounting before any promotion decision.

Drop the implicit claim that open entry is the evidence-favored window. Published evidence says the VRP is earned overnight (inaccessible to 0DTE) and the intraday component is ~zero; Vilkov finds results qualitatively unchanged across 10:00/13:00/15:00 entries, and separate condor studies favor late-day entry. Worth A/B-testing 13:00-15:30 ET entry against open entry within the same advisory lane.

Conditioning is where the published edge lives: the only net-positive 0DTE results (put ratio spreads net SR 0.93; diversified basket net 0.82) come from disciplined out-of-sample CONDITIONAL rules. The system's VIX-tercile sizing and GEX-state gating are the right architecture; consider adding asymmetric structures (put-ratio-style) to the template set instead of only symmetric straddles/condors, since ex-post 0DTE PnL loads on direction/skew more than realized variance.

GEX wings have published support as a vol-state conditioner (positive MM gamma → lower intraday realized vol, Dim-Eraker-Vilkov), but it is a dampening tendency, not a pin guarantee — treat GEX range as a sizing/abort signal, not as wing-safety proof; on negative-net-gamma days the same literature implies intraday momentum amplification (abort condition).

Seller-side profits in 0DTE are predominantly market-maker spread capture (Beckmeyer et al.: >$50M of $70M retail losses were transaction costs); a non-MM seller crossing spreads is competing for the residual ~$20M gross pool while paying the MM toll — structurally thin edge, reinforcing advisory-only status.

VIX-tercile sizing is directionally supported (VRP is strongly time-varying and the distribution state-dependent), but add an absolute circuit breaker calibrated to a VIX-65-type gap (Aug 5 2024): tercile sizing within a regime does not protect against an overnight regime jump appearing at the open.
